claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, the automorphism-aware Pollard rho in proof.md (order-6 orbits under negation and the GLV endomorphism, Teske 16-adding walk, coefficients in the Z[lambda] basis, 4096 parallel walks, chained lookup capped at 64 slots) recovers x with probability at least 0.39 using at most 2^128.749460 total target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 with C=1000, including preprocessing, the incomplete-addition reserve, verification and output. Peak memory is at most 2^136.850027 bytes. Preprocessing is at most 2^16.328837 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work. Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. Heuristics and their slack are those listed in claim.json. This is a classical cold attack, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Exhaustive collision recovery on Z/n under the same order-6 multiplier action, Z[lambda] coefficient maps, 16-branch index and 5/4 birthday budget used in proof.md. Checks the basis identity on every step. Does not establish production instruction costs, hash-chain lengths or secp256k1 field arithmetic.
